title: Replace a laser printer's toner cartridge, taking the new one's protective cover off first
instruction: Replace the toner cartridge with the new one.
context: Swapping toner is routine work for office, retail and IT staff. New cartridges ship with an orange protective cover that must come off first: left on, the cartridge won't go home. The used one goes in the return box for recycling, and the printer won't run with its door open.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. (1) Laser printer: compact mono model, 30 cm deep, 36 cm wide, 19 cm tall, grey ABS, about 6.5 kg, fixed (double-sided tape) with the centre of its base at (43, 0), its front toward the arms. Its front door (34 x 15 cm, hinged along its bottom edge, a dark finger lip at the top centre) is shut, held by a magnetic catch (about 2 N at the top edge). Behind it the cavity (31 cm wide, 13 cm deep, 6 mm of headroom over a cartridge) holds the used cartridge on two side rails; a sprung bump in the cavity floor clicks behind a rib under the cartridge's front edge when it is fully home (about 8-10 N to push past). (2) Used toner cartridge: black plastic, 30 x 10 x 9 cm, about 0.6 kg, label TONER CARTRIDGE USED on its top, a handle bar (8 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick, 2 cm proud) centred on its front face. (3) New cartridge: identical, about 0.8 kg, label TONER CARTRIDGE NEW, with an orange plastic protective cover (28 cm long, about 30 g) clipped over its top front edge, standing 12 mm above its top, with a pull tab on top. It lies in the installation orientation (handle toward the arms) on two white foam packing blocks (10 x 4 x 1 cm) with its centre at (24, -27). (4) Return box: open brown cardboard box, 13 x 34 cm inside and 10 cm deep, its front flap folded down to 4 cm, fixed with its centre at (22, 27). Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers.
scoring: Judged at the end from the video, a photo and a tape measure. Home: the new cartridge sits level on its rails, pushed fully in (within 4 mm of the back stop, past the detent's click), still for 1 s. Cover off: the orange cover is not on the new cartridge (more than 1.5 cm from its clipped position). Boxed: the used cartridge lies inside the return box, still for 1 s. Shut: the door is within 2 degrees of shut. 1.0: home, cover off, boxed and shut. 0.5: home, cover off and shut, but the used cartridge isn't in the box. 0.25: home and cover off, door not shut. 0: anything else, including the new cartridge not home (or home with its cover on), the used cartridge put back in, or any cartridge or the cover dropped off the table.
reset_notes: Put the used cartridge back home (it clicks), clip the cover back onto the new one and lay it on the foam blocks, empty the return box, shut the door.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena YAM station. The printer is an articulation: a door on a bottom hinge with a magnet (task code: a spring within 5 degrees of shut) and a sprung detent bump in the floor that the cartridge's rib clicks past. Cartridges and cover are rigid bodies with box colliders; the cover sits on by geometry and friction rather than snap clips. No toner, electrical contacts or printing.
